objective: Proof: on ordered triangulations, a counting law with one bit per edge, any triangle rule read in vertex order and any tetrahedron rule, possibly depending on orientation, satisfies the ordered 2-3 and 1-4 identities exactly when it is one of the seven symmetric laws (all 0, all 1, all equal, even cocycles, odd cocycles, even or odd, free) restricted to the triangle rule; so invariant counts are 1, 2, |H1(M; Z2)|/2 or |H1(M; Z2)|, and the twisted Fibonacci knots contribute only their constant and parity parts; exhaustive standard-library census over all 255 triangle rules.
status: Proved by TWIST-3D-20261025-001A-P001: on ordered triangulations, the counting laws with one bit per edge that satisfy the ordered 2-3 and 1-4 identities are exactly the seven symmetric laws (all 0, all 1, all equal, even cocycles, odd cocycles, even or odd, free) inside each of the 255 triangle rules, 354 laws in all, with orientation-dependent rules never differing; twists add nothing: invariant counts are 1, 2, |H1(M; Z2)|/2 or |H1(M; Z2)|, and each twisted Fibonacci knot carries only a constant law and its parity law.
title: Twists add nothing to counting laws in three dimensions
